title: Angel One Overtakes Zerodha as India's Second-Largest Broker as Groww Pulls Ahead
excerpt: NSE data for October 2026 shows Angel One added 2.43 lakh active clients to reach 69.98 lakh, passing Zerodha's 67.59 lakh, while Groww added 3.04 lakh clients and extended its lead at the top.
body:
• Angel One is now India's second-largest stockbroker by NSE active clients, with 69.98 lakh clients and a 14.97% market share in October 2026.
  • Zerodha slipped to third with 67.59 lakh active clients, down 32,435 from September, for a 14.46% share.
  • Groww stayed far ahead in first place with 1.37 crore active clients, adding 3.04 lakh in October alone for a 29.43% share.
  • For NRI investors comparing brokers, active-client rank signals scale and liquidity of the platform, not pricing or service quality — check brokerage, NRI account rules and support before switching.

Angel One has overtaken Zerodha to become India's second-largest stockbroker by active clients, according to National Stock Exchange (NSE) data for October 2026. The reshuffle ends a long period in which Zerodha held the second spot behind Groww, and it underlines how quickly India's discount-broking hierarchy is still changing.

Angel One added 2.43 lakh active clients during October, taking its active client base to 69.98 lakh and its market share to 14.97%, Entrackr reported from the NSE data. Zerodha slipped to third with 67.59 lakh active clients, down 32,435 from 67.91 lakh in September, with a market share of 14.46%.

Groww extends its lead at the top

Groww retained its dominant position with 1.37 crore active clients in October, adding the highest number of clients of any broker at 3.04 lakh during the month. Its market share stood at 29.43%, the highest among stockbrokers in India.

The Hindu BusinessLine, also citing NSE data, noted that Groww's net additions were roughly one-and-a-half times the combined additions of the next four largest brokers, and that Groww accounted for nearly 49.5% of the industry's net additions in October.

An industry still adding clients

The total active client base on the NSE increased 1.33% month on month to 4.67 crore in October, from 4.61 crore in September, an addition of nearly 6.15 lakh clients, according to the NSE data reported by Entrackr.

ICICI Securities retained fourth position with 21.64 lakh active clients, adding 3,722 during the month. Upstox held fifth spot with 18.43 lakh active clients, despite a decline of 11,348. Their respective market shares stood at 4.63% and 3.94%.

Among other major brokers, Kotak Securities added 12,895 clients to reach 14.05 lakh, while HDFC Securities' active client base increased to 13.60 lakh. Dhan added 25,739 active clients to reach 11.47 lakh, and Motilal Oswal added 7,283 to reach 9.16 lakh.

Fast growth at the smaller end

Sahi emerged as the fastest-growing broker among the top 20 in October, Entrackr reported. It added 34,372 clients during the month, taking its total to 3.15 lakh, with a market share of 0.67%.

At the other end, Paytm Money recorded the steepest decline among the top 20 brokers, losing 32,501 active clients to fall to 7.30 lakh. PhonePe's Share.Market added 7,041 active clients to reach 2.14 lakh, and IIFL Securities added 5,095 to reach 3.46 lakh.

For Indian investors abroad who maintain demat accounts back home, the October numbers are a useful reminder that the platform race is being won on new-client additions, not incumbency. Rank alone, however, says nothing about brokerage charges, research, NRI onboarding or customer support, which remain the practical factors when choosing or changing a broker.
nri_angle: For NRI investors holding demat accounts in India, the broker reshuffle is a practical prompt to compare platforms on NRI onboarding, charges and support, not just headline client rankings.
author: Diaspora Desk
